speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: It is indeed timely and critical to raise this conversation as their roles and responsibilities today have expanded well beyond merely imparting subject knowledge.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: And together with Senior Parliamentary Secretary Shawn Huang, we recently engaged union leaders from the education cluster of unions which cover unions across the entire education sector from pre-school to mainstream as well as Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs), polytechnics, universities and private education providers on the protection and well-being of teachers and educators across the education and continuing education and training (CET) ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teachers and educators today are tasked with addressing a wide range of student needs including supporting students' 21st century competencies, Character and Citizenship Education, Co-Curricular Activities, well-being as Teacher Counsellors, and many more.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: These tall orders cannot be met without enhanced support and protection for them.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: In the past four years I have persistently raised questions in this House on enhanced well-being support and harassment prevention for this group.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Through this Adjournment Motion, I hope and wish to reiterate the call to foster workplaces that uphold dignity, safety, and respect for teachers and educators through a pre-emptive, strengthened, and holistic approach, or what I call the "3Ps" of Prevent, Protect and Partner.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teaching is a work of heart, and our teachers and educators are deeply committed to taking care of students, but we cannot expect them to be accessible to parents and guardians, or even students and school leaders, round the clock, especially for non-urgent matters.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: These protocols will serve as a more school-specific and enforceable extension of the refreshed GSHP, where schools can stipulate official hours during which teachers and educators may be contacted and establish alternatives for urgent matters outside those times, in a way that best fits their own context and in consultation with all stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: These protocols will help parents and guardians as well, by preventing misunderstandings on when and how to reach out and ensuring that communication is efficient and purposeful.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Establishing these boundaries will not compromise the quality of support offered to students and families.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Most students and families use existing communication channels appropriately and thus are already respectful of these boundaries.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: And in fact, when teachers and educators can maintain work-life harmony, they return each day refreshed, prepared and engaged, benefiting students directly.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Establishing these boundaries marks a significant step towards a more balanced, supportive and sustainable education system.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: An especially vulnerable group here is preschool teachers, who have frequent interactions with parents, since parents of young children tend to be very highly involved and protective.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Young children also have higher emotional and physical needs, which can blur professional lines.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: In situations where parents disagree with teachers' handling of children displaying difficult behaviour or expect them to be overly accommodating to unreasonable requests, teachers may feel pressured into accepting disrespectful or harassing behaviour.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This is where the commitment of strong leadership to upholding guidelines and protocols is key, without which guidelines and protocols remain mere suggestions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Good practices can only take root when standards are reinforced consistently and their importance demonstrated through action.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teachers and educators need to know that school leaders have their backs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I commend the school leaders, supervisors, and superintendents that check in with their officers regularly.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I also urge them to readily empower teachers and educators to stand up against harassing or disrespectful behaviour should they occur.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: There are few cases of harassment and bullying of teachers and educators in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: However, for the minority of cases, each should be investigated seriously and without delay, with strong consequences for aggressors and compassionate support for those affected.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I urge schools to re-examine and, where necessary, strengthen their punitive measures and escalation procedures and processes.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: At the same time, we must prioritise repairing the harm caused to victims, recognising that those who have experienced harassment or bullying may suffer lasting effects on their career confidence, mental health and sense of security.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teaching is an inherently socially and emotionally demanding job, but teachers and educators should never accept disrespectful behaviour like abusive language from parents and guardians, inappropriate comments in the classroom, or unwelcome physical contact as "part of the job".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Every teacher and educator must be made aware of their rights and protections available to them to prevent underreporting and failure to seek support.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: They should feel safe to inform their school leaders or MOE, or in more severe cases where their safety is threatened, file a police report without fear of retaliation, blame or being penalised in their performance reviews.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: School leadership must also be sensitive to the implications of power dynamics and equipped to escalate the matter after mediation or formal warnings have failed.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Our teachers and educators make a vital contribution to our nation by nurturing the young minds of tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: They have the right to work in environments free from harassment, intimidation and discrimination.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We cannot risk allowing behaviour that undermines them to go unchecked.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Consequently, any accusations made should be thoroughly investigated and the accused should have the opportunity to respond.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Perhaps the Ministry can also look into conducting mandatory training programmes on recognising, preventing and healing from harassment and bullying that are trauma-informed for all school staff.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: When in doubt, teachers and educators who are union members can also approach their union for help.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Our teachers' and education unions in Singapore hear many cases of grievances a year, ranging from managing students' misbehaviour and abusive attacks from parents to work appraisals, mental health issues and career progression.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Our unions stand ready to champion all teachers and educators from trainee teachers to veteran faculty, from pre-schools to special education (SPED) schools to Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) including ITE, polytechnics, universities, private education providers and international schools as well.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: For IHLs, where parents are less involved and students more mature and motivated in pursuing their academic and career goals, the number of harassment cases may be limited.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: But even a small number of isolated cases can have serious impacts, not only on the individuals involved but rippled across the broader school community.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This dedicated office typically acts as an informal and neutral "help desk" of sorts, that provides confidential conflict resolution options and resources to faculty, staff and students that are, crucially, free from departmental influence.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: At the moment, an equivalent of such a dedicated office that acts as an unbiased and third-party channel does not seem to exist or be widely known in IHLs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Faculty, staff and students' primary recourse is to approach school leaders, human resources (HR) departments or supervisors, which may discourage reporting of sensitive or uncomfortable matters.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: A dedicated office is, thus, especially helpful for those who are not ready to pursue formal action but still want to discuss options or seek advice on navigating the system, a more flexible approach to formal HR processes.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The dedicated office's mandate can also be expanded to include proactive responsibilities, such as identifying systemic issues and recommending changes to workplace policies, standards and codes of conduct to school leadership based on case trends and feedback.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Further, access to these well-being resources should include allied educators, like school counsellors and special educational needs officers, as well as allied staff in SPED schools, like teacher aides and vocational education personnel, who may face higher physical risks and emotional strain but receive less support and protection than teachers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: It is commendable that MOE has made significant efforts to break down silos between mainstream schools and SPED schools, including increased opportunities for intermingling among children as well as attachments, rotations and secondments for teachers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I submit that MOE should ensure that Allied Educators and SPED non-teaching staff are not overlooked in the policy decisions surrounding their well-being, protection and career progression.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We often say, "It takes a village to raise a child".

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: To promote a positive school culture of mutual support and trust, we need all hands on deck.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: If our teachers and educators are not given the respect that they are due, there is a problem beyond that of individuals' actions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: It is a community problem, influenced by our shared beliefs, perspectives and practices.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The community then needs to be part of the solution.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Law enforcement agencies and community partners need to step up as well to partner with and support our educational institutions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Parents and guardians, for one, play an influential role in instilling into and reinforcing students' respect for teachers and educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: When we treat their teachers and educators with courtesy and gratitude, we inspire our children to do the same.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: If they feel misunderstood or think that something is unfair, rather than responding defensively, we can guide them to discuss these issues respectfully.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: MOE has also stepped up its efforts in engaging and cultivating strong partnerships with families by working with parent support groups (PSGs).

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Such networks help share responsibility and resources and can make a big difference in easing teachers and educators' workload.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: By simply sharing homework help or answers to straightforward questions with each other, instead of defaulting to teachers and educators as the point-of-contact, parents and guardians free up time for teachers and educators to focus on more meaningful tasks.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Schools should continue to encourage parents and guardians to reach out to their peer networks as a primary resource, leveraging technologies like an online forum or private chat group.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: PSGs can also organise more informal meet-ups, so that parents and guardians can get to know one another better and foster a sense of community.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am mindful that teachers and educators' issues can be deeply gendered, given that this is a profession disproportionately over-represented by women.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Although the profession is of course not the sole purview of women, it has a strong association with nurturing and emotional labour, roles traditionally assigned to women.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: As such, teachers and educators may be expected to perform additional emotional labour, such as comforting students and handling interpersonal conflicts without formal compensation, despite the demands on their time and energy.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This devaluation not only impacts them financially, but also the respect and recognition they receive, since it perpetuates the notion that such work is less skilled.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teachers and educators should, therefore, be fairly compensated for their extended duties in providing nurturing and emotional labour, such as teachers who take on additional caseloads as teacher counsellors.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: On a more macro level, we also want to make sure that the teaching profession is respected and appreciated by the wider community, which can help prevent and reduce the mistreatment of teachers and educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: By raising the status of teaching as an attractive, meaningful and esteemed career does not have to come from the top-down, but from within.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am, therefore, imploring school leaders to entrust teachers and educators with more autonomy over their ways of working and teaching.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This means holding space for teachers and educators to share their feedback as well as listening and taking into consideration their ideas.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teachers and educators possess first-hand and in-depth knowledge of their students' evolving needs, making them uniquely positioned to identify gaps in school programmes, culture and policies.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: We must believe they hold within themselves, the creativity and innovation to create impressive and contextually relevant ways of working and teaching that are sustainable and effective.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Partnering teachers and educators in this regard, therefore, also reflects respect and recognition of their expertise.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: To be clear, what I am suggesting is not to add yet another role onto teachers and educators' ever-growing list of demands that they also be counsellors, helpline operators, administrators, event organisers and so on.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: On the contrary, by allowing teachers and educators a say in how they work and teach, we may be able to address their perennial pain points of managing heavy workloads, burnout and poor student behaviour.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: This will allow teachers and educators' voices to be represented and allow them a seat at the table.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: When parents respect teachers and educators, their children do too.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: When school leadership trusts their officers to do what they do best – teach; it sends a powerful message about the quality and value of the profession.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I urge all relevant stakeholders in our child-raising "village" to commit to building a respectful and harassment-free workplace for our teachers and educators.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Teachers and educators, whom we make exceptional demands of, are passionate individuals who have chosen to dedicate their careers to educating our children and youths.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am confident that every single one of us in this room can think of at least one teacher or educator who has touched our lives and changed us in some irrevocable way.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The National Trades Union Congress' affiliated unions in the education cluster stand ready to champion their needs and well-being.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Let us pay their contributions forward by upholding the dignity, safety and respect for all teachers and educators, because every teacher matters, every educator matters and every worker matters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In front of the MOE building at Buona Vista stands a poignant structure: a hand gently lifting a child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This powerful image captures the essence of our teachers' calling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Every day, in classrooms across our nation, our teachers embrace the profound responsibility of "holding the future of Singapore in their hands".

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Each of us has been touched by the dedication of a teacher at some point in our lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: From kindergarten to university, these teachers shape not just our minds, but also our character.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: That is why teachers are so valued by our society and deserve our respect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We deeply appreciate the vital role that our teachers play and we are committed to supporting their well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We recognise that being a teacher comes with its own set of challenges and pressures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: All of us at MOE are deeply committed to creating a safe and nurturing environment for our teachers to flourish in their roles that they play.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: An essential part of fostering this supportive environment in our schools and MOE Kindergartens, is ensuring that our teachers are protected from any form of mistreatment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is necessary that we call out abusive, harassing and disrespectful behaviour towards our teachers and educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When our teachers or non-teaching staff face or witness an incident of workplace harassment, they should report it and approach their school leaders for advice and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Alternatively, they can also reach out to MOE HR.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is also crucial to provide a safe environment and support for the victims of harassment, as the harassment could emotionally affect our teachers and educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Professional counselling services are available to our teachers and educators, to support them in their recovery and mental wellness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Where appropriate, we also facilitate alternative work arrangements or grant leave to further support the victims in their healing process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our educators in IHLs and SPED schools have access to such support too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Private preschool operators have in place similar policies and measures to safeguard their educators' interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Early Childhood Development Agency has also put in place guidelines in preschool educators' learning frameworks to guide educators in establishing and fostering effective partnerships with parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While there are various measures and support systems in place for our educators across all levels, it is important to recognise that their ability to perform their crucial roles often depends on a support system that extends beyond the classroom and the institution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This support system includes parents and the unions, all of whom play vital roles in enabling our educators to do their job well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Parents are our key partners in nurturing our young.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These guidelines incorporate inputs from parents and educators and provide focused guidance on how schools and parents can work together in ways that matter to our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Patrick Tay suggested for schools to be clearer and more specific in outlining how parents should engage with educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is important for individual schools and their parents to develop a shared understanding and tailor the guidelines to serve the school context and the parent community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These are not one-off discussions, but ongoing conversations that our schools need to have with our educators and parents, with the support of the PSGs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Last Saturday, I joined about 200 PSG members from across about 100 schools to go through the GSHP and also other resources to better equip parents in their parenting journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The parents who were participating were very appreciative of these resources and tools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I think we should give them time to work out with the schools when school reopens next term to work out the protocols for communication between the parents and the schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I am always inspired by our PSG members' passion and commitment in supporting our children and the wider community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In many of our schools, PSGs provide mutual support and share information and other resources with fellow parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is especially beneficial for parents who are new to the school system or experiencing key milestones in their children's education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They do this typically through parent chat groups and may even step up to moderate conversations to create safe spaces for parents to share their concerns, experiences, tips and encourage one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is heartwarming to see such positive peer support in action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Parents generally appreciate our teachers and respect the boundaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Failure to do so could sap our teachers of a disproportionate amount of their attention, at the expense of other students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Another crucial element of our educators' support system is the strong partnership with teachers' unions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE HR works closely with the unions to support the well-being of our teachers and educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We hold quarterly dialogues to discuss matters such as capacity building, mental well-being support and grievance handling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The unions provide an additional source of feedback on ground issues and highlight specific cases of teachers and educators who require stronger support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The education landscape in Singapore comprises diverse institutions from preschool to tertiary level, with various stakeholders and concerns, as well as structures and processes to support their educators and teachers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: What works for MOE schools may not work for other educational institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We encourage our unions in the education cluster to continue to partner the respective educational systems and build on their existing structures and processes to enable educators to work in a respectful and harassment-free work environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Educators and teachers, whether in public or private institutions, can seek help from the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Since 2019, TAFEP has also set up the Workplace Harassment Resource and Recourse Centre which provides support —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State, you have got about half a minute left.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We understand the challenges they face and the dedication they bring to their roles every day.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Our aim is to ensure that our teachers and educators remain not just future-ready and relevant, but also resilient in the face of challenges.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Together, we can create an environment where our teachers feel respected, supported and empowered to mould the future of our nation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
